label: GPT-6 Luna

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Hey Tara, Derek Shaw from Brinewatch. So I took a look at your site and with a fleet like yours I think we can save you a ton on spoilage. We put sensors on every truck, alerts go out the second something drifts and the reporting basically runs itself.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: We actually don't have much of a fleet. Most of our boxes ship by parcel. We only run six vans for local delivery.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Oh okay, sure, well six vans is a great place to start, how do the boxes stay cold?

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Ice packs and insulated liners. The problem is the summer. Boxes sit on porches and customers open them warm.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Yeah, so our sensors can actually go right inside.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Our refund rate on warm boxes hit about 3% of boxes this summer, and the complaints hurt more than the refunds.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Totally and honestly our sensors can go right in the boxes so you'd know exactly when they warmed up, customers would see that you care.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: Hmm, at a few dollars a box, that's not going to work for us. We ship thousands of boxes a week.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Right, right, we'd figure out the pricing. The vans are easy though, every van gets a sensor and you'd see them on one dashboard.

segments.speaker: BUY
segments.text: The vans aren't really where we lose boxes. It's the last few hours on the porch.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Gotcha, well let me send you a deck with some case studies and you can see what fits.

segments.speaker: REP
segments.text: Perfect, I'll shoot that over today, thanks Tara.
